claim: Let \(G\) be a finite connected simple graph, let \(g\in V(G)\), and let \(\sigma_g(G)=\{\theta:E_\theta e_g\ne0\}\) be the adjacency eigenvalue support of \(g\). For \(d\ge2\), let \(a,b\) be antipodal vertices of the \(d\)-cube \(Q_d\), and use the standard adjacency Hamiltonian on the lexicographic product \(G[Q_d]\), whose adjacency matrix is \(A_G\otimes J_{2^d}+I\otimes A_{Q_d}\). Then perfect state transfer from \((g,a)\) to \((g,b)\) occurs if and only if \(\sigma_g(G)\subseteq\mathbb Z\). When it occurs, the complete set of positive transfer times is \(t=(2r+1)\pi/2\), \(r=0,1,2,\ldots\); in particular the minimum time is \(\pi/2\). More precisely, at an arbitrary time \(t\), such transfer is possible only if \(\cos t=0\) and \(e^{-i2^d tA_G}e_g=e_g\). This strictly strengthens the earlier sufficient condition requiring all of \(G\) to be integral. For example, let \(T\) be the seven-vertex tree with a degree-two vertex \(g\) joining two degree-three vertices, each of which has two pendant leaves. Then \(\phi_T(x)=x^3(x^2-2)(x^2-4)\), so \(T\) is nonintegral, while \(\phi_{T-g}(x)=x^2(x^2-2)^2\) and the local support at \(g\) is exactly \(\{-2,0,2\}\). Hence \(T[Q_d]\) is a connected nonintegral graph with perfect state transfer between the two antipodes in the \(g\)-fiber at time \(\pi/2\) for every \(d\ge2\).

correctness.rationale: The exact decomposition by the uniform hypercube vector reduces transfer to an orthogonal-sector hypercube equation plus \(e^{-i2^dtA_G}e_g=e_g\). Hypercube amplitudes at distances zero and one force \(\cos t=0\). The return equation then makes \(2^{d-2}(2r+1)\theta\) integral for every supported eigenvalue \(\theta\), hence \(\theta\) is a rational algebraic integer and therefore an integer. The converse and exact time set follow directly.
